frequency_question: How often do announced large-scale Treasury/Fed liquidity or debt management operations reach or exceed projected ramp-up milestones within the designated timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes major structural debt management, buyback, or liquidity injection programs initiated by the U.S. Treasury or Federal Reserve with explicitly scheduled volume expansion targets. Excludes emergency ad-hoc crisis facilities (such as TAF or emergency swap lines) which have different scaling dynamics.

cases.name: 2024 U.S. Treasury Regular Buyback Program Initiation

coverage_note: 4 named structured episodes; captures all major discretionary Treasury/Fed long-term debt restructuring and buyback scaling programs over the timeframe.
known_gaps: Excludes minor fine-tuning operations that did not feature explicit multi-billion dollar phased expansion schedules.
skeleton: Decomposed into major structural debt management scaling cycles since 2000 where initial announcements specified phased volume increases.
multiplier: 4 historical scaling cycles observed; 2 successfully ramped up to targeted operational caps within the structural window without premature termination or scaling back.
validity_reason: Debt management framework stability and institutional norms at the U.S. Treasury evolve slowly over multi-decade horizons.
